body.content: Unresolved: Can calibration analysis (Candidate 6) distinguish genuine meta-monitoring from confidence-anchoring on checklist completion? If the panel is more confident when more boxes are ticked, this is compliance-driven confidence, not calibration. But if the panel is more confident on divergence cases it gets right, this might be genuine calibration. The problem is that divergence cases where the checklist is right and the panel complies will also have high box-ticking. Need a way to decouple compliance rate from correctness.
body.possible_next_move: Examine cases where the checklist's rule is correct but counterintuitive (high compliance needed) vs. cases where it is correct and intuitive (low compliance needed).
body.why_keep_this: Identifies a confound in the calibration approach that could undermine its discriminating power.
